hold_text: Tier-2 by preparation and Tier-3 by the merge gate: src/prop/prop_executor.py decides the SIZE and the SL/TP a live bracket is typed with on the breakout_1 prop account, so it is order-path code and docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md hard-blocks a self-merge of it (Tier-3 examples: 'the live order path ... prepare + propose them as a draft PR, merge only on explicit operator approval'). APPROVAL SOUGHT FROM: the manager session session_01MM8o5js6TcDFeNAPBY4Ntv, which dispatched this lane with 'Open a HELD PR (.github/pr-landing hold, tier_2_3_needs_approval) with the evidence. The manager merges it.' The lane does not self-land it and has written no automerge request.
why:
BREAKOUT-CAP-ROUND (lane session_01PmaNf2jXagFToXuLPhZHhq, dispatched by manager session_01MM8o5js6TcDFeNAPBY4Ntv). The breakout_1 executor refused a valid $75 ticket over an 11-cent rounding overshoot.

MEASURED, THE SKIP: GET /api/bot/prop/fills?limit=1000 returns all 77 rows of prop_fills (ids 1-77, contiguous, 2026-06-22 -> 2026-10-02). Exactly ONE is lost to this reason -- id=75, ticket prop-manual-00e7ecbd6bd4 (SOLUSDT long, trend_donchian_sol_prop), status `skipped` at 2026-10-02T04:04:36Z, reason 'risk cap: resized (risk gate ENFORCE: ticket risk $75.11 exceeds the flat-mode cap $75.00 -- resized to the cap)'. The probe is POSITIVE-CONTROLLED: the same regex over the same rows finds that row, so the single hit is a measurement and not a quiet probe. COLLATERAL: the next signal's ticket prop-manual-d428ef87df61 (04:02:11Z) was then SUPPRESSED as a reticket ('outstanding_ticket:emitted: prop-manual-00e7ecbd6bd4'), so the one skip cost two signals.

MEASURED, THE ROOT CAUSE, from the ticket's own numbers (GET /api/bot/prop/tickets: entry 121.23, sl 118.59428571, qty 28.45528451, risk_usd 75.00) against SOLUSD's declared venue specs (config/prop_platforms.yaml executor.lots: lot_units 1, lot_step 0.01, price_step 0.01; config/prop_rulesets/breakout_routing.yaml cvpp 1.0):
  1. size_lots floors 28.45528451 -> 28.45 lots. At the ticket's RAW prices that is 28.45 x 2.63571429 = $74.99 -- UNDER the cap. The lot-step flooring is innocent.
  2. bracket_from_ticket then rounds the prices to price_step 0.01, which moves the stop 118.59428571 -> 118.59 and WIDENS the stop distance 2.63571429 -> 2.64.
  3. risk is recomputed from the TYPED values (correctly -- that is the whole point of `ticket_risk_usd`): 28.45 x 2.64 x 1.0 = $75.108 -> $75.11.
So the overshoot is introduced by the executor's own PRICE rounding, AFTER the quantity was decided, and it is bounded by one price step: at this size, up to 28.45 x 0.01 = $0.28. Reproduced exactly in-process (both numbers, $75.11 before and $74.98 after, are asserted in the tests).

WHY IT KILLED THE TICKET: evaluate_guards appends ANY enforce_ticket_cap action other than 'unchanged' to `reasons`, so `fits` goes False. prop_risk_gate.enforce_ticket_cap is pure and merely REPORTS what enforce mode would do to the size (`action: resized`, `risk_usd: 75.0`); nothing ever applied it. The announced resize was never real, and the reason string said 'resized to the cap' on a row where nothing was resized and the ticket was dropped.

THE FIX, in two parts, both in src/prop/prop_executor.py:
  (a) bracket_from_ticket applies the $-cap WHERE THE SIZE IS DECIDED, after the price rounding, by re-deriving the quantity from the TYPED stop distance through the SAME size_lots that already rounds DOWN to the venue lot step and re-checks min_lots: 28.45 -> 28.40 lots, risk $74.98 <= $75.00. One more lot step (28.41 x 2.64 = $75.0024) would breach the cap, so the cut is to the last size that fits, not to a round number.
  (b) THE CUT IS BOUNDED BY WHAT THE TICKET ITSELF ASKED FOR -- `requested` = the ticket's own qty x its own un-rounded stop distance x cvpp. A ticket asking for more than the cap is NOT resized; it reaches the guard over-cap and is REFUSED there, as now. This is the bright line: the executor repairs its own typing artifact and never silently re-sizes a trade nobody sized. `min(...)`/floor semantics mean the size can only ever go DOWN, never up.
  Also fixed in the same function, because the division in (a) needs it and the hole is real: a stop that rounds ONTO the entry is now REFUSED ('no stop distance to risk'). Before, risk read 0.0 and every cushion guard would have passed a position with no effective stop.
  And the guard's refusal text for a genuinely over-cap ticket no longer says 'resized' -- reading that word on a skipped row is what made this take a whole investigation.

TESTS (tests/test_prop_executor.py, 7 added/changed; the two the dispatch asked for are the first and the third):
  - test_venue_increment_overshoot_is_resized_down_and_placed: the REAL ticket's numbers; asserts lots 28.45 -> 28.4, risk_usd_before 75.11, ticket_risk_usd 74.98 <= cap, guards v.fits True with NO risk-cap reason at all and checks.risk_cap.action 'unchanged'.
  - test_one_more_lot_step_would_have_breached_the_cap: pins that 28.41 would not fit, so the cut is the last fitting step.
  - test_a_gross_over_cap_ticket_is_still_refused_never_resized: a ticket asking $120 with no rounding involved -- risk_cap_resize is None and the guard REFUSES.
  - test_the_size_never_grows: a ticket well under the cap is typed as sized; the floor is never walked back up.
  - test_no_declared_cap_still_refuses_rather_than_emitting_an_unbounded_size: cap None resizes nothing and still refuses (an unknown cap bounds nothing).
  - test_a_stop_that_rounds_onto_the_entry_is_refused_not_risk_zero.
  - test_risk_gate_enforce_cap_refuses_above_flat_75 (pre-existing): updated to the new, honest refusal wording; it still refuses the same $80 ticket.
The pre-existing fixture declares no price_step for SOLUSDT, so every other test in the file is untouched by the price rounding and the new tests declare their own stepped symbol.

VALIDATED: python3 -m pytest tests/test_prop_executor.py tests/test_prop_sizing_mode.py tests/test_prop_risk_gate.py tests/test_prop_breach_guards_report.py -q -> 278 passed, 136 skipped. `ruff check .` with CI's own pin (requirements-dev.txt ruff>=0.15.0,<0.16; ruff 0.15.22) -> All checks passed. (A locally-installed ruff 0.16 reports 193 pre-existing findings repo-wide because 0.16 expanded its default rule set -- that is the exact reason requirements-dev.txt upper-bounds it, so the pinned version is the one that matters.)

SCOPE / RISK: two functions in one file, plus tests. No config/**, no deploy/**, no src/runtime/orders.py, no strategy params, no risk-cap VALUE anywhere -- the flat $75 cap is unchanged and still read from breakout.yaml sizing.flat.max_risk_usd. The $75 flat ticket risk on breakout_1 is SETTLED operator policy and is not reopened here; this PR only makes the executor PLACE AT that cap instead of dropping the ticket for being 11 cents over it. The direction of the change is strictly DE-RISKING at the venue: the size it types is smaller than the one the ticket asked for, never larger.

MERGED / DEPLOYED / OBSERVED: merged -- no (this is a HELD PR; the manager merges). Deployed -- no. Observed -- no, and that is tracked rather than assumed: pipeline row PI-20261002-ULPHZHHQ-0001 clears only when the FIRST resize-path ticket is seen PLACED in prop_fills (status open/filled with facts.risk_cap_resize != null). The absence of further 'risk cap' skips is explicitly NOT accepted as evidence, because a quiet period looks identical to a working resize. REVERT: revert this one commit; the executor returns to refusing the overshoot, which is the pre-PR behaviour and loses tickets rather than risking money.
